question: The settlement: where does the cash finally settle, and in what kind of money?
answer: In most of what the library holds, the cash still settles in money that already existed. Swift's ledger coordinates commitments among 17 listed banks, 8 of which have a completed pairing located; final settlement happens afterwards through existing payment systems. Of the 12 market systems, 1 settles in central-bank money by the master's own description (Sterling Fnality Payment System), 4 move banks' own tokenized deposits, and for 7 the master does not say. Who finances the interval before settlement: banks validated funding and managed the interval before external settlement. Customer availability can precede bank cash receipt.

walk: Evidence: 17 initial-use participants; six completed pairings across eight banks located through September 9. Nine banks have no completion receipt located.
Framework: published shared governance and regulated participation; executed participant terms remain unreviewed.
Operator: SWIFT runs coordination; participating banks retain money and settlement responsibility.
Issuer: participating banks retain deposit liabilities; SWIFT does not issue this money.
Funding: SWIFT describes upfront confirmation; the precise reservation or credit object remains undisclosed.
Coordination: SWIFT operates the shared commitment ledger on Besu/EVM software.
Clearing: UOB and HSBC report matched and netted obligations before external settlement.
Cash: FAB reports completed correspondent settlement outside the SWIFT ledger.
Customer clock: DBS reports a September 5 weekend USD payment in minutes; external-finality timing is not specified.
Failure: executed participant terms, loss allocation and stressed performance remain unresolved.

rows.title: Who is bound?
cells: Identify the legal entity, jurisdiction and applicable domestic implementation before assigning a bank requirement.
Which rule applies to this entity, account and date?
Basel standards are not themselves supranational law.

rows.title: Bank buffers & stable funding
cells: LCR examines a 30-day stress horizon; NSFR examines stable funding over a one-year horizon.
Which assets and funding qualify, and what is transferable?
Neither ratio establishes capacity to execute a particular intraday payment.

rows.title: Payment timing & credit
cells: Track opening resources, incoming flows, deadlines and the largest cumulative shortfall.
Who supplies the interval when incoming money is late?
Daily totals conceal peak funding needs; public data gaps do not prove missing internal monitoring.

rows.title: Prefunding, netting & withdrawal
cells: System rules determine release, position limits, queues and whether funding can leave.
Can this balance fund another payment here—and can it be withdrawn elsewhere?
CHIPS reuse does not confer unrestricted outward withdrawal. SWIFT does not inherit CHIPS rules.

rows.title: Turn assets into funding
cells: Separate asset market value, accepted collateral value and remaining credit capacity.
Is the asset eligible, pledged correctly and fundable before the deadline?
A tokenized fund share does not automatically inherit the collateral treatment of its underlying securities.

rows.title: Holder rights & exit
cells: Redemption depends on the holder, issuer, jurisdiction, procedure and payout route.
Who can redeem, into what, how much and when?
Token transfer, issuer processing and bank availability are separate events.

rows.title: Quotes & available inventory
cells: A route needs a willing counterparty or available exit inventory at the requested size and price.
Who replenishes the liquidity after a one-way flow?
24/7 access and atomic execution do not guarantee price or unlimited capacity.

rows.title: Failure & replenishment
cells: Test late receipts, collateral markdowns, unavailable funding and counterparty failure.
Who still owes payment, and what can be delayed or released?
A successful pilot is not proof of stressed capacity or loss allocation.

sections.title: FedNow, Fedwire and the payment rails (21 dated records)
sections.sub: Every row of the money record's rails track, plus the rows on other tracks that name FedNow or Fedwire, newest first.

rows.title: Section 301 Turns on Another Country's Payment Rails — the Brazil Action
cells: USTR/Executive Office of the President · Notice

A Presidential Memorandum of Jul 15 (FR Doc. 2026-14654, published Jul 20) directs Trade Act section 301 action on Brazil's acts, policies and practices related to Digital Trade and Electronic Payment Services, alongside tariffs, intellectual property, ethanol and deforestation. USTR's companion Notice of Action published the same day (FR Doc. 2026-14542, 91 FR 45516). Read plainly: American trade coercion is now pointed at a foreign country's national electronic payment system. Pix is a sovereign rail; section 301 is the lever.

rows.title: FedNow's Third Birthday — 1,800 Banks, $271B a Quarter, and a Ceiling Raised Twentyfold
cells: Fed360's anniversary item puts numbers on the public rail: 1,800+ live institutions, up from about 1,600 in January; seven of the ten largest U.S. banks aboard; Q1 2026 volume 2.7 million transactions worth $271.3 billion; reach claimed at over half of all American checking and savings accounts. The line worth keeping is the ceiling: launched at $500,000, lifted to $1 million in March 2025, lifted again to $10 million in November 2025. A retail instant-payments service does not need a ten-million-dollar transaction limit. That is a wholesale rail wearing a consumer coat.

rows.title: Perli Speech — Repo Market Structure, Tokenized Repo, and Stablecoin-Driven Reserve Demand
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Speech

Roberto Perli (NYIC/Markets Group) discusses tokenized repo transactions, stablecoin-driven reserve demand, and collateral efficiency from instant settlement. The vocabulary: 'tokenized reserves,' never 'CBDC.' The NY Fed's innovation arm keeps building while renaming the work.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

rows.title: Logan Calls for FOMC to Voluntarily Centrally Clear Its Operations
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas — Lorie Logan · Speech

At the NY Fed Future of Market Liquidity workshop, Dallas President Lorie Logan called for the FOMC to voluntarily centrally clear its open market operations (Treasury buys/sells and repo), even though the SEC clearing mandate does not apply to the Fed. Also flagged blockchain potential to integrate market segments and speed collateral flow. Extends her September 2025 TGCR proposal and April 2026 liquidity blueprint — the Fed re-plumbing itself onto the new infrastructure.

rows.title: FedNow at Three — the Fed Lays ISO 20022 Track Toward Cross-Border, and Sits Down With the Private Clearing House
cells: Chief FedNow Executive Nick Stanescu's three-year Q&A names four things coming to the Fed's own instant rail: FedACH payee-name verification exposed to FedNow users by API; enhanced ISO 20022 message formats 'that will lay the groundwork for the FedNow Service to enable cross-border payments'; a request-for-payment pilot; and Federal Reserve Financial Services co-chairing a newly established X9 Fraud Forum jointly with The Clearing House. Read the last one twice. The Clearing House is the private rail owned by the biggest banks — RTP, the thing FedNow was built to compete with — and the Fed is now its co-chair on a shared standards body. The public rail and the incumbents' rail write the fraud rulebook together. Same absorption grammar as Cede & Co. surviving the DTC rewrite and Visa/Mastercard keeping their own book.

rows.title: Financial Data Transparency Act Joint Data Standards (nine agencies)
cells: Treasury, Fed, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB, FHFA, CFTC, SEC · Final Rule

Nine agencies adopt one machine-readable language — common identifiers (LEI, FIGI) — for all the data the financial regulators collect. The government standardizing its ledger language, the quiet precondition for supervising a tokenized system at machine speed.

rows.title: CFTC RFC: 24/7 Trading of Standard Futures and Perpetual Contracts
cells: Commodity Futures Trading Commission · Proposed Rule

The CFTC asks how US futures markets could run around the clock — and says the quiet part in Questions 7-9: how does margin settle 'when traditional payment systems such as Fedwire and CHIPS do not operate,' and what 'stablecoin or other tokenized settlement asset' fills the gap? A federal agency, in the Federal Register, admitting the dollar's official rails sleep and asking private tokens to work the night shift.

rows.title: The Desk Absorbs the Tokenization Lab (Chung, 'Evolving Market Structure')
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Speech

The new head of the NY Fed's markets desk confirms the Innovation Center now reports up through the same group that implements monetary policy, that the Fed remains in Project Agorá as it moves to real-value testing, and that Cedar and Pine were the groundwork. The word 'CBDC' appears nowhere; the work continues as 'tokenized reserves.' The dollar's operating desk rehearsing for token money, out loud.

rows.title: CFTC RFI: Removing Barriers to Fintech Partnership With Market Infrastructure (EO 14405)
cells: Commodity Futures Trading Commission · Proposed Rule

Under EO 14405, the CFTC hunts through its own rules for anything that keeps fintech firms from plugging into regulated market infrastructure, and asks how to streamline their registrations. The de-walling of the perimeter, run as an executive-order homework assignment.

rows.title: KC Fed Frames Kraken Account as Payment-Account Pilot
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City · Supplemental Disclosure

The Kansas City Fed published a supplemental document framing the Kraken Financial limited-purpose account (granted March 4, 2026) as a pilot of the Reserve Bank payment-account concept — the first live test of the prototype the Board proposed in FR 2026-10375. Only overdraft-rejecting services (Fedwire Funds) are available; neither the Kraken exchange nor other Payward subsidiaries get access. The pilot generates real-world data for the payment-account rulebook whose comment period closes July 27, 2026.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City

rows.title: Regulation J — FedNow Cross-Border via Intermediaries
cells: Amends subpart C of Regulation J to let FedNow participants use non-Reserve-Bank intermediaries (e.g., correspondent banks) to send funds transfers — explicitly to support private-sector cross-border payment solutions, with FedNow handling the U.S. domestic leg. The instant-payment rail reaching for the border.

rows.title: Standing Repo Facility — Aggregate Limit Removed, Full Allotment (FedTrade Plus)
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Operating Policy Statement

The Desk removes the aggregate operational limit on standing overnight repo operations and moves them to a full-allotment format on the new FedTrade Plus platform (one proposition per security type per operation, $40B max each). The Fed's overnight dollar backstop, formerly capped, is now effectively unlimited — and rebuilt on new rails. Announced Dec 10, effective Dec 11, 2025; a companion note flags a move toward central clearing of the facility.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

rows.title: Fedwire & National Settlement Service to Expand to 22x6 (toward 22x7x365)
cells: The Board announces Fedwire Funds Service hours will expand to 22 hours/day, 6 days/week (Sunday–Friday), with National Settlement Service tracking it — an interim step toward round-the-clock 22x7x365 settlement, implementation expected 2028–2029. The wholesale dollar plumbing moving toward always-on, to defend the dollar's global role.

rows.title: Treasury Turns On FedNow for Federal Disbursements (Digital Payout)
cells: Bureau of the Fiscal Service · Announcement

The Fiscal Service enables FedNow for federal agency payouts — eight-plus agencies live, FEMA pushing disaster money instantly instead of mailing checks. The state itself now pays citizens over the Fed's instant rail: Treasury and Fed plumbing fused at the retail edge, the completion of the EO 14247 arc.

rows.title: The ESF Steps Into Argentina: the Emergency Fund Goes Abroad Again
cells: Treasury announces an exchange-stabilization operation in Argentine pesos through the Exchange Stabilization Fund — the same statutory pocket that holds the gold certificates and sits ready for any revaluation play. The quiet fund is awake and working.

rows.title: Fed Board Approves Fedwire and NSS Operation on Sundays and Holidays (22x6)
cells: The Board formally decides the central bank's settlement day will no longer respect the weekend — Fedwire and the National Settlement Service expand to Sundays and holidays, implementation no earlier than 2028, with full seven-day operation left on the table. The precondition for 24x7 markets settling in central-bank money.

rows.title: FedNow Transaction Limit Raised Tenfold, to $10 Million
cells: Federal Reserve Financial Services · Press Release

The instant-payment rail's cap jumps from $1 million to $10 million (effective November 12). With the average payment already past $100,000, FedNow stops being a retail toy and becomes a wholesale-adjacent rail.

rows.title: Fedwire Completes the ISO 20022 Migration in One Cutover
cells: The $4.7-trillion-a-day wire system cuts over to the global structured-data standard in a single shot, no coexistence with the legacy format. The dollar's main artery now speaks the same machine language as every payment system on earth — richer data for programmability, screening, and interop with tokenized rails.

rows.title: Request for Information on Potential Actions To Address Payments Fraud
cells: Treasury Department — Comptroller of the Currency · Notice

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Treasury; the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (Board); and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) seek public input on questions related to payments fraud. This request for information (RFI) offers the opportunity for interested stakeholders to identify ways that the OCC, the Federal Reserve System (FRS), and the FDIC could take actions collectively or independently in their varying respective roles to help consumers, businesses, and financial institutions mitigate check, automated clearing house (ACH), wire, and instant payments fraud.

rows.title: Standing Repo Facility — Morning Operation Added (BNY Tri-Party)
cells: Federal Reserve Bank of New York · Operating Policy Statement

Adds a daily early-morning (8:15–8:30am ET) standing repo operation alongside the existing 1:30pm one, settling on the BNY tri-party platform, then still under the $500B combined cap. Effective June 26, 2025 — the step that preceded December's uncapping: the Desk re-timing and re-plumbing the repo backstop through 2025.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

rows.title: Project Pine: the Fed Pre-Builds a Tokenized Control Panel
